# Resolver fixture provenance

These four small authored TypeScript texts are inert compiler inputs, never imported or evaluated by tests. Both entry fixtures use the existing SDKs. The helper declaration is at line 2, column 14; its deliberately invalid initializer produces TS2322.

`tests/project/resolver-fixtures.ts` builds complete raw project inventories. Its synthetic trusted toolchain selection is supplied separately from the lock and does not attest to installation. Pin bodies and raw hashes use an independent Node crypto implementation of the documented versioned identity bodies. Generated BMPs use an explicit 54-byte header and padded BGR rows; generated PNGs use the existing pinned encoder. No downloaded images or third-party source fixtures are needed.

The existing `tests/assets/fixtures/jpeg/baseline.jpg` is read by reference. It is a 32x24 Pillow/libjpeg fixture described by `tests/assets/generate-jpeg-fixtures.py`; SHA-256 is `4dcf67435bdf1475b7deab281cb5ac292a9d79d2c26185f16e7c5649b85eab3c`. It is not regenerated during tests. An initial jpeg-js encoder trial did not meet the existing decoder's entropy-padding policy; that failed trial remains in the worker evidence, and production codec policy is unchanged.

The default package has a literal independently calculated pin golden: manifest SHA-256 `6249a3334986aac809139e5d584b6169211fc33ed28b3579207e41eaeb082950`, content SHA-256 `823529bfa4dcec07ddd5ae7e369d87a28631813d6aa6f5ff47ecd115c36999aa`. Fixture text readers deliberately select LF for this known package body; separate raw-content tests preserve and distinguish BOM/CRLF inputs without normalization in the resolver.

Quota fixtures establish valid inputs at exactly 8 MiB local source, 32 MiB vendored originals plus raw manifest, and 16 MiB project image originals. The latter uses 21 maximum BMPs, a 256x256 BMP, and a 1x1 PNG with a bounded inert tEXt chunk and valid CRC. Four binding originals total exactly 1 MiB at lengths 393270, 393270, 196662, and 65374; the last is a padded 1x1 PNG. Two compressed 512x512 PNG bindings establish exactly 2 MiB decoded RGBA while originals remain below 1 MiB; adding a separate 1x1 image adds four RGBA bytes.

Metadata rejects the 33rd closure file, 65th asset record, fifth alias, next original binding/project-asset byte, and next per-image byte before resolver decoding. These are explicit reuse evidence. Package/source raw-byte checks have independent reachable equality/overflow fixtures. Canonical source paths cannot collide across individually valid registered local directories, nor within a valid package inventory: metadata enforces disjoint case-folded registries and unique case-folded inventory paths. The case-collision test therefore asserts the earlier authoritative rejection without invented owners. Cross-definition asset aliases remain a reachable enrichment case and assert both exact owners.
